rv.q: Perhaps the way to refer to this “Monte Cristo” is not so much as an adaptation but as fan fiction.
Taking in this Monte Cristo, observers wouldn’t be blamed for feeling as if they were not in 2026 but back in 1926 and having a sufficiently agreeable time of it.
Unfortunately, what remains in their version is Disneyfied Dumas—a story that replaces dramatic tension with family-friendly humor, and malevolent motives with saccharine songs.
It is one of the most accomplished musical productions to be seen currently in NYC.
For all its ambition, Monte Cristo presents a strong, impressive debut—one that occasionally struggles to reconcile its tonal shifts but never lacks for theatrical sweep or conviction.
Monte Cristo misses both the novel's romanticism and its propulsive energy.

cn.t: This operetta-style adaptation of Dumas's epic tale draws mixed reviews, with critics divided on its old-fashioned approach and struggle to condense the sprawling source material into a cohesive two-hour musical.
